references.authors: Fatehi Hassanabad A, Sinha S, Jaffer A, et al.
references.claim: Human pericardial macrophages suppress cardiac fibrosis through cystatin C signaling after myocardial infarction, demonstrating that macrophage-derived signaling can directly regulate fibroblast fibrotic activity.
references.contribution: This proposal extends the macrophage-fibroblast communication question to synovial fibroblast-macrophage cocultures and tests whether the direction and mediator specificity of signaling are feed-forward and pathway-specific.
references.limitation: This work is in the pericardial/cardiac context, not synovial tissue, and does not test directional signaling in coculture.
references.title: Human pericardial macrophages suppress cardiac fibrosis through cystatin C signaling after myocardial infarction

references.authors: Mosallanejad K, Hubeau C, Schwartz Sterman A, Tan Y
references.claim: Macrophages and fibroblasts engage in bi-directional crosstalk that is essential for transient matrix remodeling and physiological healing, but sustained activation under inflammatory conditions drives maladaptive repair and fibrotic remodeling.
references.contribution: This proposal tests whether the direction and mediator specificity of macrophage-fibroblast crosstalk in synovial cocultures are feed-forward and pathway-specific, extending the review's framework to a testable experimental design.
references.limitation: This is a review article that summarizes the field but does not provide original experimental data on directional signaling in synovial cocultures.
references.title: Macrophages and the Tissue Repair Circuit: Homeostasis, Autoimmune Diseases, and Resolution-Based Therapeutic Strategies

references.claim: In difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis, reciprocal stromal-myeloid signaling forms a self-sustaining 'non-resolution switch' that locks the synovium in a chronic state, with pathogenic fibroblast subsets sustaining inflammation and driving tissue damage.
references.contribution: This proposal tests whether the direction and mediator specificity of macrophage-fibroblast crosstalk in synovial cocultures are feed-forward and pathway-specific, extending the failed-resolution framework to a testable experimental design.
references.limitation: This is a review article that summarizes the field but does not provide original experimental data on directional signaling in synovial cocultures.
references.title: Failed resolution as a mechanistic basis of difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis: stromal-myeloid crosstalk in the synovium and emerging resolution-restoring therapies
